title: Peek does not work after being idle

judgment.rationale: The report has a clear state transition: Peek stops responding after idle and opening PowerToys restores it. The process lifecycle has a concrete reliability defect: launch_process has no success result and assigns hProcess after ShellExecuteExW, making stale or invalid process state plausible.
evidence: Space activation fails for CSV, text, and Markdown after idle.
Opening PowerToys from the taskbar restores activation.
launch_process does not return success and process-handle assignment is not guarded by the ShellExecuteExW result.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the fork-side lifecycle-hardening design, with diagnostics requested if reproduction disproves the process-state hypothesis.

fix_assessment.rationale: A lifecycle recovery fix is plausible and localized, but the idle duration and exact failure state remain unknown.

proposed_fixes.title: Recover Peek activation after idle
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Peek can retain stale or unverified viewer-process state after idle; activation trusts that state or launch failure instead of validating a live process and recovering the viewer.
plan: Make launch_process return an explicit success/result and only retain a process handle after successful ShellExecuteExW.
Make is_viewer_running validate the handle/process and clear stale state.
In on_hotkey, recover by relaunching or reinitializing the viewer when the process is absent or unresponsive, then signal activation only after the event is ready.
Add structured lifecycle logging for launch, stale-handle cleanup, and recovery; preserve normal single-instance behavior.
verification: Reproduce after a measured idle interval with CSV, text, and Markdown.
Confirm Space activates Peek without opening Settings.
Retest repeated activation, viewer exit, sleep/resume, and disable/enable.

confidence.rationale: Recovery behavior and lifecycle code align with the symptom, but no diagnostic confirms whether the viewer exits, hangs, or loses its invoke event.

issue_context.summary: Peek ignores Space after an unspecified idle period until PowerToys is opened from the taskbar.
known_information: No comments, diagnostics, assignee, or linked fix.
information_gaps: Viewer process state and logs immediately after failure.

design.root_cause: Viewer lifecycle state is not validated and recovered robustly around launch and hotkey activation.

implementation_steps.change: Return launch status, guard handles, and clear dead process state.
implementation_steps.code_shape: bool launch_process(); if (!ShellExecuteExW(...)) return false; m_viewerProcess = sei.hProcess; return true;
edge_cases: Viewer exits between validation and signal.
tests: Lifecycle unit tests where possible; logging assertions.

implementation_steps.change: Recover viewer before signaling invoke event.
tests: Idle, exit, resume, repeated hotkey tests.

verify: Run manual idle and sleep/resume matrix.
risks: Aggressive recovery could create duplicate viewers.
alternatives: Only refresh hotkey registration: rejected until process state is ruled out.
Always launch on hotkey: rejected because it risks duplicate viewers.

fork_trace.note: Fork-only design mirror; no upstream action implied.

adversarial_review.conclusion: No blocking objections; collect idle-failure diagnostics during implementation if lifecycle validation does not reproduce.
